review_note: Read the test and helper-b31no-oracle.R line by line. The oracle is independent: hand-built Henderson tabular A of an inbred pedigree (diag up to ~1.7), base-R dense Laplace (helper-sb26) at the fitted parameters, SD vectors built by hand from fitted coefficients and non-palindromic selector grids; the pedigree provider is compared with the hand A, so it is a real independent construction. Slope rows are fitted as unlabelled animal(1 + x | id) with one SD formula per coefficient, which is exactly the 'independent animal fields' layout the rows name (no correlation claimed). Gamma intercept row is animal(1 | id, pedigree) with sd ~ w0. Each of the six row_keys has a matching test (Poisson A and Ainv, NB2 Ainv and pedigree, Gamma I and Ix pedigree). Sensitivity: swapped coefficient sets, reversed SD, flipped selector, K by position, K x2, cov2cor(K) each asserted > 0.1 against 1e-4 agreement; observed min gaps 0.19 to 3.8, agreement 1e-9 or better. Hashes of test, helpers, R/src sources, console log, manifest and receipt all recompute correctly (receipt sha matches the fragment). Console log: 6 blocks, 124 expectations, 0 failures, 0 skips, 2 optimiser NA/NaN warnings. Rerun on Totoro cores 280-285 reproduced 6/124/0/0/0 with 2 warnings. Does NOT establish: calibration, coverage, recovery or Julia parity; any estimated cross-coefficient correlation (labelled animal blocks); behaviour beyond one seed per route; the Gamma shape/NB2 size are taken at fitted values, not checked as estimates.
